question: What is the primary clinical use of an intradermal injection?
explanation: Intradermal injections are used mostly for diagnostic tests like tuberculosis screening and allergy checks because they allow slow absorption in the skin layer. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why do medications absorb very slowly from the dermal layer of the skin?

options.A: The epidermis blocks most medications from entering.
options.B: Sweat glands actively wash the medication away.
options.C: Skin cells in the dermis are tightly packed together.
options.D: The dermis has a very limited blood supply.

explanation: Limited blood vessels in the dermis mean the drug stays localized and is picked up very gradually by the body. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which skin layer receives an intradermal injection?
explanation: The needle is inserted into the middle layer of the skin, known as the dermis, which sits right beneath the outer epidermis. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why is the inner forearm a preferred site for routine tuberculosis skin tests?

options.A: It is hairless and allows easy visual inspection of the reaction.
options.B: It has a higher concentration of blood vessels for rapid results.
options.C: It contains thick subcutaneous fat that cushions the needle.
options.D: It absorbs medications much faster than other body parts.

explanation: The inner forearm provides a clear, accessible area with minimal hair, making it simple for nurses to read skin changes accurately. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h2)

question: What size syringe is standard for administering an intradermal injection?
explanation: A 1 mL tuberculin syringe allows accurate measurement of the very small doses used in intradermal injections. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which needle gauge range is most appropriate for an intradermal injection?
explanation: Fine needles between 25 and 27 gauge are thin enough to enter the superficial skin layers with minimal trauma. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the correct needle insertion angle for an intradermal injection?
explanation: A very shallow angle of 5 to 15 degrees keeps the needle in the superficial dermal layer instead of slipping deeper. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h4)

question: What visual sign confirms that an intradermal injection was successfully placed in the dermis?

options.A: A small bleb or blister forms on the skin surface.
options.B: The surrounding skin turns pale and cold to the touch.
options.C: A drop of blood appears at the injection site immediately.
options.D: The medication leaks back out through the needle track.

explanation: The formation of a raised bleb proves the fluid is trapped within the tight dermal skin layers. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h4)

question: When should a nurse evaluate the skin reaction for a tuberculosis skin test?
explanation: Tuberculosis skin reactions take time to develop, so the immune response is most accurately measured between 48 and 72 hours later. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h5)

question: What specific characteristic of a skin test reaction must the nurse measure?
explanation: Induration refers to the hard, raised swelling caused by cellular immune activity, which is the true indicator of a positive test. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h5)

question: What happens to a diagnostic skin test if the nurse accidentally injects the medication into the subcutaneous layer?

options.A: The medication crystallizes under the skin and causes infection.
options.B: The patient develops immediate anaphylactic shock.
options.C: The reaction becomes much larger and easier to read.
options.D: The test becomes invalid because the drug absorbs too quickly.

explanation: Subcutaneous tissue has more blood supply, causing rapid absorption that ruins the localized delayed immune reaction needed for a valid test. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h6)

question: What important detail must be included when documenting an intradermal injection?

options.A: Brand name of the alcohol swab

explanation: Recording the exact location is necessary so the healthcare team can find the correct spot when returning to read the test results. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h7)

question: Why should a patient be instructed not to scratch or scrub a tuberculosis skin test site?

options.A: It can irritate the skin and cause false readings.
options.B: It forces the medication to enter the bloodstream instantly.
options.C: It causes the needle mark to bleed heavily.
options.D: It washes away the skin pigment permanently.

explanation: Scratched or irritated skin can cause swelling and redness that mimics a positive immune response, leading to misdiagnosis. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h7)
